A1.justification: Both complete, readable 30-page PDFs describe the same FairCrowd research. The main text, equations, figures and Appendices A–G can be matched reliably; v2 additionally contains Appendix H.

before.justification: Section 5 and Figures 2–4 report original synthetic experiments and evaluations on Crowd Judgment and Jigsaw Toxicity.

after.justification: The original experiments remain, and Appendix H/Figure 5 adds original results on Measuring Hate Speech.

M1.justification: Section 4 and Algorithm 1 correct the stated tie-handling threshold from (2π_a+s_aβ*)/(2π_a) to (π_a+s_aβ*)/(2π_a), aligning it with the unchanged Theorem 4.1. This is a localized correction to the written procedure; the PDFs do not establish that the implementation changed.

E1.justification: v2 retains the synthetic, Crowd Judgment and Jigsaw evaluations and adds Measuring Hate Speech, with gender-target sensitive groups and class/group imbalance. This is a focused extension of the existing binary crowdsourced classification coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the existing experiments is unchanged. Figure 5 extends the existing FC-versus-Post TD comparisons over Majority Vote, Bayesian aggregation and Dawid–Skene; Bayes_Count denotes the already described counting-based Bayesian estimator. FairTD's exclusion on the added dataset does not remove an existing comparison.

E3.justification: The added hate-speech experiment specifies ε values of {0.05, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2}. Existing experiments retain their settings, and the new evaluation uses the established F1-versus-demographic-parity protocol with 60% test sets.

E4.justification: Appendix H adds a targeted robustness check under class and sensitive-group imbalance, supported by Figure 5. This is a limited additional robustness question; the existing synthetic analyses of competent, adversarial and nearly uninformative annotators remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report variability using ten resampled test sets and shaded regions described as variance. Figure 5 follows the same practice; v2 does not introduce a new uncertainty estimator, significance test or increased run count.

E6.justification: Figure 5 adds F1–demographic-parity curves on Measuring Hate Speech. The accompanying text reports FC as competitive with Post TD and observes larger variability across resampled test sets. The existing result plots in Figures 2–4 are unchanged.

T1.justification: There are localized mathematical edits, including correction of the variance expression near Proposition 3.6. Proposition D.3 changes γ_R from 1−α_R−β_R to (1−α_R−β_R)/R, but its subsequent derivative calculation still requires the former definition, introducing an inconsistency. The principal theorems and proof structure are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same central claims: fairness bounds and convergence, extension to discrete inputs, and FairCrowd's fairness guarantees and empirical effectiveness. The added benchmark supplies further evidence without redefining those claims.

C2.justification: v2 interprets the new experiment as suggesting stability under severe class and group imbalance despite greater variability, and Appendix H explains why F1 is preferable to accuracy in this setting. Existing interpretations and the limitation concerning feature-dependent annotator behavior remain.

D1.justification: The implementation paragraph corrects the threshold documentation and removes the zero-order characterization while retaining sequential quadratic programming and existing hyperparameters. v2 also documents the new dataset's sensitive attribute and FairTD's 30-hour timeout, and newly acknowledges a source of experimental code.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kennedy et al. (2020) for Measuring Hate Speech and removes Prabhakaran et al. (2021), Wei et al. (2022), and the associated CIFAR-10N discussion. Positioning relative to Denis et al., Gao et al. and Li et al. remains substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized copyedits, standardizes the FairCrowd name, updates the publication and contribution footnotes, and adds conflict disclosure and acknowledgements. Appendix D receives clearer subsection headings, while the overall narrative and section order remain stable.

P2.justification: v2 adds Figure 5, corrects the algorithm name in Figure 1, and reformats Algorithm 1 with an explicit Output line. Equation 14 and surrounding text reflow, but Figures 2–4 retain their original plotted content.

improvement.justification: The added imbalance experiment broadens empirical support, and the corrected Algorithm 1 threshold improves reproducibility. However, v2 introduces a γ_R normalization inconsistent with the subsequent proof of Proposition D.3, weakening the written support for a central convergence argument. These benefits and the unresolved theoretical inconsistency prevent a confident net quality judgment.
